legal.aboutIntro: Nexa is a small chat service run by one person. Below are the same Terms and Privacy Policy you agreed to when you created your account (version {version}).
legal.encryptionBody: Your messages, files, and calls are encrypted on your device before they are sent, using keys the server never has. I cannot read them, I cannot monitor them, and there is no switch that would let me. The only things I can actually see are your public profile (things like your username, display name, avatar, banner, and about me), the basic delivery details the server needs to work (who sent what, where, and when), and public images like emoji and stickers.
legal.enforcementBody: Since chats are encrypted, I cannot see what anyone says in messages, files, or calls, so I do not go looking. The exception is usernames, avatars, and banners. Those are public, so they are the only things I moderate directly. Anything else only comes up if I receive a valid legal order, and even then I can only share what the server actually holds. Message text, file contents, and call audio still cannot be handed over, because I have no way to read them.
legal.gateCheck: I have read the Terms and the Privacy Policy, and I agree to the rules.
legal.gateIntro: One quick thing before you continue. Please read and agree to the Terms ({version}). The short version: your messages are encrypted so nobody here can read them, including me.
legal.gatePrivacy: No email, no phone number, nothing sold, nothing tracked. The Privacy Policy lists exactly what the server keeps.
